title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (cote 147, the structure at infinity of M_{g,ν}). Y = D_0 is a smooth modular multiplicity (stack/orbifold) carrying a normal-crossings divisor Θ, here the boundary of the compactified moduli stack. For each stratum one has the normalized closed stratum D (with a local immersion, étale over a stratum D_i of Y), its open part D^* (complement of the deeper strata) and an object P_D over D. P_D is presumably the punctured tubular neighbourhood, a torus-type bundle of 'small loops' around the branches. Its restriction is P_{D^*} = P_D|D^*.

For a specialization D'' → D' (D'' deeper, mapping into the closure of D'), the previous page announces a canonical 'generalization' morphism (231) γ_{D'',D'}: π1 P_{D''*} → π1 P_{D'*}. It also notes the trivial map (232) i_{D'}: π1 P_{D'*} → π1 P_{D'} induced by the inclusion.

This page states the commutativity requirement (234): i_{D'} ∘ γ_{D'',D'} = (trivial map π1 P_{D''} → π1 P_{D'}) ∘ i_{D''}. Grothendieck warns about a key difference:
- The composite i_{D'}γ is 'of trivial nature'.
- γ itself comes from no morphism of spaces P_{D''*} → P_{D'*}, since the image of D'' in D' lies precisely in D' \ D'^*.

So γ is a genuinely homotopical specialization (exit-path type) map, from data near the deeper stratum to data over the open shallower stratum.

The construction principle for (231) begins here. Take a local immersion of smooth spaces (analytic, or multiplicities) D' → Y, coming in the situation at hand from D' →(étale) D_i → Y = D_0. One introduces, independently of Θ, the 'tubular neighbourhood of D' in Y'. This is a germ of a space containing D' itself, not its image. It therefore 'unfolds' the self-crossings of the image; the next page illustrates this with a nodal curve and its thickened band.

The next page explains the framework:
- Germs of differentiable manifolds around D', unique up to unique isomorphism.
- For differentiable or topological multiplicities, germs of topoi defined via pro-pointed systems of manifolds.

Presumably γ is then obtained by deforming loops near D''^* into the tubular neighbourhood of D' and pushing them off to D'^*.
errors: No mathematical error on this page.
The previous page's (233), transcribed as π1 P_{D'*} → π1 P_{D'}, should be π1 P_{D''*} → π1 P_{D'} (the composite of (231) and (232)); this is consistent with the diagonal of (234).

The 'évident' morphism P_{D'} → P_{D''} mentioned on the previous page would induce π1 in the opposite direction to the bottom arrow of (234). Either the transcription is off or the arrow direction is loose; the intended bottom arrow is presumably induced by P_{D''} landing in (a neighbourhood version of) P_{D'}. This is unresolved from the image.

ideas.what: Generalization morphism π1 P_{D''*} → π1 P_{D'*} between fundamental groups attached to a deeper stratum and to the open part of a shallower stratum of a normal-crossings boundary. It is not induced by any map of spaces.
ideas.modern_name: specialization/generalization maps in the stratified fundamental groupoid; exit-path category (link of deeper stratum → shallower stratum)
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (exit paths, unpublished 1990s), Treumann 2009, Lurie (Higher Algebra, appendix); in the moduli context, Ihara–Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps 'lego'
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the structure at infinity of M_{g,ν}, tubular neighbourhoods and the 'Teichmüller tower', but not these explicit maps as far as I know.

ideas.what: Commutativity of the square relating γ with the inclusion-induced maps i_D
ideas.modern_name: compatibility of the exit-path functor with the inclusion of open strata into neighbourhoods

ideas.what: Tubular neighbourhood of a local immersion D' → Y, defined as a germ of a space around D' itself (unfolding self-intersections), independently of the divisor. Extended to multiplicities as germs of topoi via pro-systems.
ideas.modern_name: tubular neighbourhood / normal bundle of an immersion; germs of stacks; deformation to the normal cone
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical differential topology (Whitney, Milnor) for immersions; for stacks, folklore
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions a theory of tubular neighbourhoods for stratified structures (dévissage of stratified spaces), without details.

missed.claim: A plan to define the generalization maps of the fundamental groupoid at infinity of M_{g,ν} via 'unfolded' tubular neighbourhoods of local immersions of strata, as germs of multiplicities/topoi. It anticipates the exit-path formalism in a stacky setting and is only sketched in these notes.
missed.quote: la flèche γ_{D'',D'}, qui ne correspond à aucun morphisme P_{D''*} → P_{D'*} (NB l'image de D'' dans D' est contenue justement dans D'∖D'^* !)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The construction itself is now standard (exit paths, tangential base points). It documents Grothendieck's early stratified/exit-path viewpoint on the Teichmüller tower, which is of historical rather than technical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: Sound and conceptually nice: specialization maps not induced by space maps, and unfolded tubular neighbourhoods of immersions. However, these are now standard ideas (exit paths, tubular neighbourhoods, tangential base points), and the page only states requirements and begins a construction.
